title: Siena nos. 20 and 23: a captain at Perugia to King Ladislaus, and two royal memoranda on the Marche campaign, spring 1413 (one key, ciphertext-only)

steps.what: The existing siena1421 collection survey records unsuccessful homophonic/null-aware attempts on nos. 20 and 23; this contribution does not rerun or claim those attempts.
Transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra, as confirmed by George Lasry. Shared key applied to nos. 20 and 23; subsequent image and editorial review retained uncertain passages.

Imported the current CTTS snapshot and latest edited lines; 4,254 cipher occurrences, 59 observed classes. Preserved CLEAR1-CLEAR4, tentative Sforza and Paolo Orsini, repeated Name6, and the unresolved Eucebio reading.

Used the supplied keys-and-sources report and independently checked Fermo’s April 1413 parallel, Minuti’s Sforza account, Meister pp. 51 and 55–57, and later Mazzone camp records. Spring 1413 and the identities remain proposed; 1421 belongs to another Siena piece. Comparable Lucca Sforza sign is post-recovery support, not the matched alphabet.

Only R4811 CTTS L6-L10 mechanically decoded: 322 signs yield 328 literal letters matching the normalized current edition, with no spelling emendation. Refreshed the visual key and English translations. Full editions remain editorial readings, not a full mechanical validation.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 322 tokens, 40 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.126 per letter; random keys -4.009 (z 7.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.749 (mean -2.785, z 21.8); annealer on the real text -2.443. Verdict: pass.
Report (17 Oct 2026): no. 23 transcribed by George Lasry in CTTS; no. 20 by a detector trained on no. 20 with his ResNet model, corrected in CTTS.
Report: key recovered by Claude via crib testing and dragging on the two sheets, ciphertext only; refined by Lasry with CTTS.

Report: 'both sheets read in full (c. 4,260 symbols, one key with nomenclator)'; 60 signs, eleven nulls, seven name signs ([Paolo Orsini?], [Sforza?], [Tartaglia?] and four unidentified); dated spring 1413 from the contents and the Fermo chronicle.
This project: the report's section filed verbatim (lasry_report.md); outcome, credits and page reconciled with it; PR #41's GPT-6 Astra attribution kept in the record as a discrepancy to ask about.

Listed every Concistoro 2308 record on DECODE through the API: keys R4746-R4789 (fasc. 1, 44 records) and ciphertexts R4790-R4814 (fasc. 2, 25 pieces), matching George's survey. R4783 has no image even with a logged-in session.

Re-checked the earliest Siena keys against the seven reference signs: R4746 (1433 alphabet, Fortebraccio), the R1858 key photos, and R4747's three slips. None holds #, fat, o+, ovo, Fom, ta or e. R4747 slip 3 is a phrase code of c. 1419-21 about Tartaglia ('+° = q(ue)sta brigata d(e) Sforça'), a different system whose circle-and-cross Sforza sign parallels o+ and Meister's 1412 Viviani sign.

Read the Fermo chronicle entry for April 1413 on the page image (Cronache fermane p. 39): 'timebat maxime conte ..... ad furcam preste, Sforza cum gentibus suis ad Caldarolam et Sarnanum'; the edition itself leaves the count's name blank. Minuti (Vita di Muzzo Attendolo Sforza) names the king's reinforcements to Sforza against Paolo Orsini in 1413: 'el sig. Malatesta da Cesena, el conte de Carrara'. As the Malatesti are named in clear in no. 23, the Conte di Carrara is a contextual candidate for Name3 (ovo); not established.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.126; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.443 Scope: deliberately selected R4811 L6-L10 only, not the full key or edited texts. 328 literal letters become 325 scored letters under the model normalization.

outcome.method_basis: Report, 17 Oct 2026: key recovered by Claude via crib testing and dragging from the two sheets, refined by Lasry with CTTS; no interlinear decipherment, clear copy or matching filed key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.json: 4,023 certain non-null assignments / 4,066 non-null occurrences; excludes 41 uncertain name/reference occurrences, 2 erased tokens, and 188 provisional nulls. Coverage is not coherent-reading accuracy.

credits.note: With CTTS and Claude, 15-17 Oct 2026: no. 23 transcribed in CTTS, no. 20 by his ResNet detector corrected in CTTS, key recovered by Claude via crib testing and dragging and refined in CTTS; both sheets read in full, translations and dating. First filed through PR #41 (17-18 Oct 2026), which said 'transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra'; English translations and checks there by Codex.
credits.source: Email and report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026

gaps.item: Seven reference/name signs (#, fat, o+, ovo, Fom, ta, e) and historical identities/year
gaps.detail: No key on DECODE holds these signs: George's report surveyed the 44 Concistoro 2308 fasc. 1 keys, and the c. 1412-33 ones (R4746, R4747, R1858) were re-checked 18 Oct 2026; R4783 has no image on DECODE. The R4747 phrase slip ('+° = questa brigata de Sforça') and Meister's Viviani nomenclator both tie a circle-and-cross sign to Sforza, supporting o+ = [Sforza?]. Minuti names 'el conte de Carrara' beside Sforza in the 1413 Marche pursuit (a candidate for Name3), and the Fermo chronicle edition has a lacuna at the corresponding place ('conte ..... ad furcam preste'). Proposals only, for George's review.

gaps.item: Erasures, dessut, essereme, Eucebio, prout, closing abbreviation and subscription
gaps.detail: Uncertain or editorial passages remain in the current readable editions.

gaps.item: Nulls, compound segmentation and editorial emendations
gaps.detail: Occurrence-level verification of the CTTS transcription against the original leaves; the DECODE photographs are the only images and already the basis of George's edition. Selected five-line agreement is not whole-text validation.

outcome.notes: Credit and class follow George Lasry's consolidated report of 17 Oct 2026 ('both sheets read in full'); PR #41's material (edited lines, five-line mechanical check, visual key, validation) is kept. fraction_read is PR #41's measured key coverage; seven name signs and the subscription of no. 20 stay open.

prior.where: None known: no decipherment on the records, no matching filed key among the 44 key records surveyed (R4783 not inspected), no external copy of the plaintexts (report and PR #41); the Fermo chronicle and Minuti give the events, not the text.

human: George Lasry transcribed no. 23 in CTTS, corrected no. 20's detector transcription (his ResNet model) in CTTS, refined the key Claude recovered by crib testing and dragging, and wrote the readings, translations and dating (report, 17 Oct 2026). PR #41 (17-18 Oct 2026), filed before the report, described the same work as 'transcribed with CTTS, then solved by GPT-6 Astra' and was prepared by Codex (English translations, five-line check, visual key). The credit follows the later, consolidated report; the discrepancy is a question for George (NOTES).
